value: 24 h of caterpillar-feeding vibrations alone lowered the concentrations of most phytohormones in leaves relative to control plants given no vibrations
method: 24 h playback of Pieris rapae caterpillar-feeding vibrations to a leaf of each Arabidopsis plant through a speaker contacting the leaf with wax; control a silent sham (dowel on a foil-covered rubber base attached to the leaf)
conditions: Col-0 wild type; three plants per chamber, each on its own independently driven speaker; one vibration level (recorded feeding vibrations), so no threshold is measured; phytohormone sets N = 12 sets of three plants (Methods)

source.authors: Body MJA, Neer WC, Vore C, Lin C-H, Vu DC, Schultz JC, Cocroft RB, Appel HM
source.title: Caterpillar Chewing Vibrations Cause Changes in Plant Hormones and Volatile Emissions in Arabidopsis thaliana

where: Abstract and Methods, Frontiers full text (CC BY 4.0)
quote: We showed that feeding vibrations alone caused a decrease in the concentrations of most phytohormones, compared to those found in control plants receiving no vibrations.
note: Substrate-borne vibration without wounding or oral secretions. Same paper also tests vibration combined with wounding and methyl jasmonate, where results were more complex.

value: 24 h of feeding vibrations alone raised beta-ionone and lowered methyl salicylate in emitted volatiles; wounding plus methyl jasmonate alone lowered benzaldehyde and methyl salicylate
method: 24 h playback of Pieris rapae caterpillar-feeding vibrations to a leaf of each Arabidopsis plant through a speaker contacting the leaf with wax; control a silent sham (dowel on a foil-covered rubber base attached to the leaf)
conditions: Col-0 wild type; three plants per chamber, each on its own independently driven speaker; one vibration level (recorded feeding vibrations), so no threshold is measured; volatile collection at 22 C; volatile N not carried because two reads of the Methods gave different counts

source.authors: Body MJA, Neer WC, Vore C, Lin C-H, Vu DC, Schultz JC, Cocroft RB, Appel HM
source.title: Caterpillar Chewing Vibrations Cause Changes in Plant Hormones and Volatile Emissions in Arabidopsis thaliana

where: Abstract and Methods, Frontiers full text (CC BY 4.0)
quote: Feeding vibrations alone caused an increase in β-ionone and decrease in methyl salicylate, and wounding + MeJA alone caused a decrease in benzaldehyde and methyl salicylate.
note: Volatile emission by the vibrated plant, a response to a vibration cue; the abstract notes the levels of some VOCs were influenced by the treatments.

value: seedlings grown better after pre-sowing exposure of seeds to a 45 mT static magnetic field for 90 min than unexposed controls
method: Seeds exposed pre-sowing to static magnetic flux densities of 44.59, 146.22 and 302.53 mT (measured means) for 30, 60, 90 or 120 min, then germinated at 21 C; each density and time used a repeated (four times) exposure of 25 seeds, plus an unexposed control scored as 100
conditions: Tested range 45 to 300 mT and 30 to 120 min is the limit of the stimulus set; exposure at about 22.7 C

value: wild-type plants shortened petioles and reduced leaf blade length and width after one week of wind-forced mechanical agitation
method: constant mechanical force from stationary fans applied twice a day for 15 min for 7 days to plants 20 days after germination (6 to 13 true leaves, no floral bolt); control trays shielded from the stimulation by cardboard boxing
conditions: Col-0; 449 plants from six trays with wild type and sdg8 in each (8 to 15 plants per genotype per tray); one fan regime, so no threshold is measured

quote: The morphological traits altered included a shortening of petiole length and a reduction in leaf blade length and width (Figure 1C).
note: Wild-type response only; the paper reports no percentages for it. The sdg8 mutant responded differently.

value: etiolated wild-type seedlings were responsive to ambient elevated temperature (29 C) in hypocotyl growth
method: seedlings grown in the dark at 22 C for 3 days, then transferred to 29 C or kept at 22 C for 4 days; hypocotyl length measured
conditions: Col-0 on half-strength MS medium with 1.2% sucrose; seeds stratified at 4 C for 4 days; Figure 1 legend gives n = 27 per bar; only 22 and 29 C were compared, so these are the limits of the stimulus set; no numeric lengths in the text
